newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvia, Russia move closer to border deal.
newsitem.headline: Latvia, Russia move closer to border deal.

text.p: The Baltic state of Latvia said on Wednesday it had moved closer to settling a long-running border dispute with huge neighbour Russia by recognising the line of the frontier.
Latvia and Russia have been arguing over their mutual border since the Baltic state quit the former Soviet Union in 1991.
Latvia wants Russia to recognise a 1920 peace treaty and border deal under which Soviet Russia guaranteed the independence of the first Latvian state.
Twenty years later, Latvia and fellow Baltic states Estonia and Lithuania were annexed by the Soviet Union.
A foreign ministry spokesman said agreement had been reached during talks in Moscow to deal with the treaty and the border delimitation as two separate issues.
"This will be a purely technical agreement, which is to determine the actual border between the two countries," the spokesman said.
Latvian and Russian delegations will start a next round of talks in Riga on March 20.
"Both sides have proved that they wish to move forward dynamically," the spokesman added.
Latvia has still not officially given up a claim to some 1,200 sq km (463 sq miles) of territory, which belonged to it when it was first independent.
